pages.name: One box per position
pages.text: A valve that steers oil is drawn as a row of boxes. Each box is one position it can take. Only the box in line with the ports joins them. Each solenoid brings in the box beside it. Four ports and three boxes make this a [[4/3 valve]]. Here three boxes sit in a row, with the four ports P, T, A and B against the middle one, labelled 4/3.

pages.name: Count the positions
pages.task: How many positions does this valve have?
pages.why: Two boxes make two positions. With four ports, its label is 4/2. An intermediate switch works the same way. Its links run straight through in one position and cross over in the other.

pages.name: Slide the boxes
pages.text: Inside the valve, a grooved shaft called the [[spool]] slides in a fixed body. The row of boxes stands for it. The ports never move. Shifting the valve slides the row until another box sits against them. Energise -Y1 and the box beside it comes in. P joins A, B joins T, and the rod comes out. Here -Y1 is energised and the left box sits against the ports. Oil runs from P to A and from B to T, and the rod is coming out.

pages.name: Springs bring it back
pages.text: A zigzag at each end is a [[spring]]. With both solenoids off, the springs push the middle box back against the ports. So the sheet draws the valve with its middle box against the ports. A notched bar is a [[detent]]. It would hold the valve in whatever box you leave it. Here the springs have pushed the row back, so the middle box sits against the ports with both solenoids off.

pages.name: Let go of the lever
pages.task: You push both levers to the left box and let go. Which valve stays in the left box?
pages.answer: The one with the notched bar
pages.why: The springs push the first valve back to its middle box. The detent holds the second wherever it was left. It stays in the left box until someone moves the lever.
pages.alt: Two lever valves, one above the other, each of three boxes. The first has a zigzag at each end. The second has a notched bar at its end. The first sits in its middle box, and the second in its left box.
options: The one with zigzags at its ends
The one with the notched bar

pages.name: The middle box
pages.text: The middle box decides what happens at rest. Closed blocks all four ports, so the rod holds. With a fixed pump, its oil then goes over the relief valve. Closed keeps full pressure at P, ready for other valves. P to T sends the oil back to the tank at low pressure. That spares the pump from pushing against the relief valve. Float lets the load move the rod. Here the P to T centre is in place. The rod holds, and the pump unloads to the tank.

pages.name: Read the centre
pages.task: Both solenoids are off and the pump runs. What do the cylinder and the pump do?
pages.answer: The rod holds, and the pump unloads to the tank
pages.why: The line joins P to T, so the pump's oil returns to the tank at low pressure. The bars block A and B. The oil in the cylinder has nowhere to go, so the rod holds.

pages.name: Held is not sealed
pages.text: A closed box is drawn sealed. A real spool leaks a little between its ports. So a cylinder holding a load can creep. The symbol shows the ideal valve, not its leaks. Here the creep is sped up. Here the Closed centre holds the load, and the rod has crept a little back in, below the mark where it stopped.

pages.name: Will it hold?
pages.task: The load must stay up all night. Does the closed centre make sure of that?
pages.answer: No, the spool leaks, so the load can creep down
pages.why: The closed box blocks the ports on paper. In the real valve, oil leaks slowly past the spool, so the load can creep down. A load that must not move needs a valve that seats tightly, such as a check valve. It also needs a mechanical prop before anyone works under it.

pages.name: The other valves
pages.text: Other valves use the same boxes and marks. A 3/2 has three ports and two positions. A 5/2 for air has five ports. A relief valve opens to the tank when pressure beats its spring. A check valve lets flow one way only. Here six cards are open, each a symbol with its name and its job: 3/2, 5/2 with its ports numbered, relief, reducing, check and flow control.

pages.name: Slide the 3/2
pages.task: -Y1 is energised. Where does the supply at P go?
pages.why: -Y1 brings in the box beside it, whose arrow joins P to A. Switch it off and the spring brings back the box that blocks P and empties A to T.
